Department's own regulations, which adopt verbatim sec. 2(b) of E.O. 11514. Hearings are also required by E.O. 11644, sec. 3(b), requiring "adequate opportunity for public participation in the promulgation of such regulations and in the designation of areas and trails under this section." Hearings are especially appropriate in this case because of the admitted lack of information about the precise impacts of ORV use, and because Interior Department regulations represent a long-range policy decision that directly affects all uses of public lands.
As noted above, the new draft statement cannot substitute for the impact statements that must be filed when regulations are issued governing particular federal lands. In those cases specific impacts will be involved, and it will be important to identify them with as much precision as possible. Hearings should also be held on those statements. Public participation in the process of preparing them is necessary in order to insure that local impacts are properly identified and controlled, and that users of the public lands in question can offer their specialized knowledge of local conditions.
If the Secretary's Memorandum is final and not subject to change, this draft statement should be withdrawn and the entire matter of preparing a statement of the environmental impacts of ORV use deferred until Interior Bureaus issue detailed regulations. Unless the Secretary changes his memorandum, this statement can serve no useful purpose, and in fact is likely to result in actions harmful to the environment if taken as a guide to policy.
